description: About Northern Trust. . As a global leader in innovative wealth management, asset servicing, asset management and banking services, Northern Trust (Nasdaq: NTRS) is proud to guide the world's most successful individuals, families, corporations and institutions. . Since 1889, we have aligned our efforts with our three guiding Principles That Endure: Service, Expertise, and Integrity. Together, they reflect the three cornerstones of business conduct which we strive to instill in our employees, whom we call partners, and to provide to our clients and the communities we serve worldwide. . With more than 135 years of financial experience and over 24,000 partners, we serve the world's most sophisticated clients using leading technology and exceptional service. . ROLE SUMMARY. Northern Trust Asset Management (NTAM) is a trillion-dollar investment management firm entrusted by investors around the globe to help them navigate changing market environments so they can confidently realize their long-term objectives.. The Pricing and Valuation function is responsible for valuation oversight, fair value governance, pricing controls, valuation methodologies, regulatory reporting, and associated activities across NTAM's clients, accounts, and funds. This role will report to the Global Head of Valuations and play a key role in supporting NTAM's valuation framework through the oversight of valuation methodologies and models, review of complex and illiquid securities, and support of valuation governance processes, including committee reporting and pricing oversight activities.. The role combines valuation analysis and model oversight with governance, committee support, pricing oversight, and valuation process improvement activities.. The successful candidate will contribute to the continued evolution of a world-class Pricing and Valuation organization by identifying, developing, and championing initiatives that enhance valuation capabilities, strengthen governance and controls, improve automation and reporting, and support compliance with evolving regulatory and accounting requirements.. . PRIMARY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES. As a member of the Pricing and Valuation team, drive excellence across valuation oversight, fair value governance, and model management activities supporting NTAM clients, accounts, and funds. Responsibilities include:. Perform day-to-day valuation oversight activities related to fair valuation, ASC 820/FAS 157 leveling determinations, valuation methodology reviews, and associated reporting processes. Develop, maintain, enhance, and document internal valuation models used to support the fair valuation of complex and illiquid securities. Perform independent reviews and challenge assessments of third-party valuation models, methodologies, assumptions, and outputs to ensure valuations are reasonable, supportable, and consistent with industry practices. Research and analyze complex valuation matters including private investments, contingent value rights (CVRs), escrow positions, proxy securities, delisted securities, suspended securities, and other hard-to-value investments requiring fair value determinations. Support the Pricing and Valuation Committee (PVC) through preparation of analyses, valuation recommendations, governance materials, methodology approvals, and periodic committee reporting. The Senior IT Auditor, Information Technology (IT), is responsible for conducting and documenting audits throughout the Corporation. This role leads audit project teams, which includes providing oversight to the audit team and communicating results of the engagement to management. The Senior IT Auditor provides technical cyber expertise and training to auditors within the engagement audit team and works closely with Audit Managers to confirm the scope of the audit and to devise an appropriate testing approach to be performed during the engagement.. Principal Responsibilities. Establishes and develops strong working relationships and open communication with key stakeholders. Provides training, coaching, and auditing expertise to the audit team. Accountable for own assignments and holding others accountable for theirs including proactively managing expectations. Identify and assess technology risks and related internal controls. Plan and lead IT audit engagements across technology, cybersecurity, governance, and operational areas. Establish audit scope, objectives, timelines, and resource requirements based on risk. Evaluate the design and operating effectiveness of IT processes and controls. Coordinate with other audit teams and subject matter specialists to ensure appropriate audit coverage. Apply professional skepticism and sound judgment when evaluating processes, controls, and risk management practices. Review audit workpapers and documentation for quality and compliance with audit standards. Communicate audit progress, results, findings, and recommendations to stakeholders and Audit Services management. Maintain relevant technical and audit knowledge through ongoing professional development.. Skills / Experience. Minimum of 4-5 years of IT audit, technology risk, or related systems experience. Strong knowledge of IT audit methodologies, technology and cybersecurity risks, internal controls, and applicable standards. Ability to assess the design and operating effectiveness of IT, application, security, and technology-related controls. Broad understanding of IT infrastructure, applications, data, cloud technologies, and technology governance. Strong analytical, problem-solving, organizational, and business judgment skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines. Excellent written and verbal communication, interpersonal, and leadership skills, with the ability to work effectively with diverse stakeholders and independently or as part of a team. Relevant professional certification, such as CISA, CISSP, or equivalent, preferred.. Working Model: Hybrid (#LI-Hybrid). We have a balanced hybrid working model to ensure you get the flexibility you need, and the successful candidate will spend their time between working in the office and working from home.. Northern Trust provides a comprehensive benefits package including retirement benefits (401k and pension), health and welfare benefits (medical, dental, vision, spending accounts and disability), paid time off, parental and caregiver leave, life & accident insurance, and other voluntary and well-being benefits. title: Regulatory Change Quality Assurance Specialist
description: About Northern Trust. . As a global leader in innovative wealth management, asset servicing, asset management and banking services, Northern Trust (Nasdaq: NTRS) is proud to guide the world's most successful individuals, families, corporations and institutions. . Since 1889, we have aligned our efforts with our three guiding Principles That Endure: Service, Expertise, and Integrity. Together, they reflect the three cornerstones of business conduct which we strive to instill in our employees, whom we call partners, and to provide to our clients and the communities we serve worldwide. . With more than 135 years of financial experience and over 24,000 partners, we serve the world's most sophisticated clients using leading technology and exceptional service. . . Job Description. About the Role. . Are you an experienced assurance, testing, or controls professional who enjoys improving processes, strengthening controls, and helping business partners achieve better outcomes?. Northern Trust is seeking a Quality Assurance Specialist to join the Regulatory Change Assurance Hub within the Global Regulatory Change Management (GRCM) Department.. Reporting to the Head of Regulatory Change Assurance (Toronto, ON), this role is responsible for performing independent quality assurance reviews of key Regulatory Change Management controls, processes, data, and technology. The successful candidate will assess whether critical regulatory change management activities are operating as intended, identify opportunities for enhancement, and provide practical recommendations that strengthen regulatory outcomes across the organization.. The role requires a balanced and pragmatic professional who can provide constructive challenge while building strong partnerships with stakeholders.. In addition to conducting quality assurance reviews, the individual will support Senior Regulatory Change Assurance Managers in the execution of reviews of new or amended regulations recently implemented by the organization and assist with audit, regulatory examination, and remediation closure activities.. Major Duties. Conduct independent quality assurance reviews of key Regulatory Change Management controls, processes, systems, and data to assess whether regulatory changes are being identified, assessed, managed, and reported effectively. Perform targeted assessments of regulatory implementation activities to determine whether regulatory outcomes were achieved, and the solutions are likely to be sustainable. Provide practical review, challenge, and advice to GRCM Department senior management to ensure their initiatives and deliverables to ensure they meet the standard of independent testing functions. Evaluate the quality, completeness, accuracy, and reliability of regulatory data, management reporting, records, and supporting documentation used throughout the Regulatory Change Management process. Assess the adequacy of regulatory monitoring, horizon scanning, applicability assessments, Rules Inventory governance, system interfaces, and other critical GRCM activities. Execute assurance methodology, perform detailed analysis, and document conclusions using a consistent and evidence-based methodology. Identify weaknesses, process inefficiencies, data quality concerns, and governance gaps and develop practical, risk-based recommendations for improvement. Support the execution of Regulatory Change Assurance reviews by assisting with planning, evaluation, evidence gathering, workpaper documentation, and observation development. Assist with monitoring and verification of remediation activities to determine whether identified observations can be appropriately closed. Draft observations and recommendations, providing practical, risk-based guidance and partnering with stakeholders to develop achievable and sustainable resolution plans. Prepare high-quality reports, presentations, memoranda, and closure assessments suitable for senior management, Internal Audit, Compliance, and regulatory audiences. Support the maintenance and enhancement of assurance methodologies, testing approaches, templates, and reporting processes. Monitor emerging issues, risk themes, and lessons learned to help strengthen Regulatory Change Management processes and controls across the organization. Participate in special projects and departmental initiatives as assigned.. Skills/Experience. Experience performing quality assurance reviews, control testing, compliance testing, internal audit reviews, risk assessments, or similar assurance activities within the financial services industry. Strong understanding of control frameworks, governance processes, risk management principles, and regulatory compliance programs. Demonstrated experience evaluating the design and effectiveness of controls, identifying gaps, and assessing the adequacy of supporting evidence. Strong analytical and investigative skills with the ability to review complex processes, data, and documentation and develop objective conclusions. Ability to identify practical and risk-based solutions that improve processes while maintaining appropriate independence. Excellent written communication skills, including experience drafting testing results, observations, issue validation assessments, audit responses, regulatory responses, or remediation closure packages. Strong verbal communication skills with the ability to engage professionally and constructively with stakeholders at all levels of the organization. Experience managing multiple assignments simultaneously while maintaining strong attention to detail and meeting deadlines. Demonstrated ability to exercise sound judgment, challenge respectfully, and work collaboratively across functions. Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and experience working with workflow, governance, risk, compliance, or regulatory technology platforms.. Preferred Qualifications. Experience in Internal Audit, Compliance Testing, Quality Assurance, Operational Risk, Regulatory Compliance, Regulatory Change Management, or related disciplines. Knowledge of regulatory change management processes, regulatory inventories, regulatory obligations management, governance frameworks, or controls programs. Experience supporting audit issue validation, regulatory remediation programs, or closure assessments. Experience translating or analyzing regulatory requirements. Professional certifications such as CIA, CISA, CPA, ACA, ACCA, CRCM, or equivalent are preferred but not required.. . Working with Us. . As a Northern Trust partner, you will be part of a flexible and collaborative work culture, which has a strong history of financial strength and stability. Employees around the world give their time and talent to work for the greater good of their communities. . Reasonable Accommodation. . title: Manager, Transformation Performance and Finance
description: About Northern Trust. . As a global leader in innovative wealth management, asset servicing, asset management and banking services, Northern Trust (Nasdaq: NTRS) is proud to guide the world's most successful individuals, families, corporations and institutions. . Since 1889, we have aligned our efforts with our three guiding Principles That Endure: Service, Expertise, and Integrity. Together, they reflect the three cornerstones of business conduct which we strive to instill in our employees, whom we call partners, and to provide to our clients and the communities we serve worldwide. . With more than 135 years of financial experience and over 24,000 partners, we serve the world's most sophisticated clients using leading technology and exceptional service. . The Manager of Transformation Performance and Finance will establish the financial, performance-management and benefits-realization disciplines required to ensure that the Wealth Management transformation portfolio delivers its commitments. This manager will create a single, reliable view of investment, resource utilization, delivery performance, adoption, client and field outcomes, and realized value. . Reporting to the Head of Transformation Enablement, the manager will oversee data and financial analysts and partner with Finance, Strategic Planning, Capital Management, Procurement, Technology, Product, Program Management and initiative leaders. The role will manage the full financial lifecycle of transformation activity, including annual planning, capital and expense budgets, forecasts, software and vendor costs, consulting arrangements, capitalization and utilization, reallocations, accruals, benefits tracking and executive reporting. . This is a hands-on management role with enterprise visibility. The manager will not merely report historical results. The manager will challenge assumptions, identify performance gaps, improve the quality of decisions, and recommend actions when initiatives are over budget, underutilizing approved capital, missing milestones, failing to adopt, or not producing the intended client, field, operational or financial benefits. . Key Responsibilities. . Transformation Performance Management. . Design and own the integrated performance-management framework for the transformation portfolio, covering delivery, financial performance, client outcomes, advisor and employee impact, adoption, service, risk, controls and benefits realization. . Define standard KPI dictionaries, calculation methods, baselines, targets, data sources, owners, reporting frequency and escalation thresholds. . Create portfolio dashboards and executive reporting that distinguish activity, outputs, adoption, outcomes and realized benefits. . Establish a disciplined monthly performance review process and surface initiatives requiring intervention, additional evidence, reforecasting, scope change or discontinuation. . Ensure reporting is decision-oriented, concise and traceable to authoritative financial and operational data. . . Benefits Realization and Value Assurance. . Create and maintain benefits records for each transformation initiative, including expected client, field, growth, revenue, expense, productivity, capacity, risk and service outcomes. . Validate benefit assumptions, baselines, timing, dependencies and accountable business owners before investment approval. . Monitor whether delivered capabilities are adopted and whether adoption is producing the expected outcomes. . Partner with initiative and business owners to define corrective actions when benefits are delayed, overstated or not supported by evidence. . Coordinate post-implementation reviews and maintain a clear line of sight from approved business case through realized value. . . Budgeting, Forecasting and Financial Planning. . Lead annual and multi-year financial planning for the Transformation Office, including capital, operating expense, software, vendors, consulting, data, technology and internal resource requirements. . . Coordinate transformation inputs to strategic planning, annual budgeting, quarterly forecasting and capital-planning processes. . Maintain initiative-level and portfolio-level budgets, forecasts, commitments, actuals, accruals, variances and estimate-at-completion views. . Develop scenario analyses and recommendations to support sequencing, funding tradeoffs, capacity decisions and portfolio reallocation. . Ensure financial plans reconcile across Transformation, Finance, Technology, Procurement and business records. . . Capital Governance and Utilization. . Monitor approved capital, release schedules, capitalization eligibility, utilization, in-service timing and forecasted carryover in partnership with Finance and Accounting. . Identify underutilized, delayed or stranded capital early and recommend acceleration, reallocation, reforecasting or release. . Ensure initiative teams understand approved funding boundaries and provide timely evidence supporting capitalization and financial controls. . Prepare capital-governance materials and maintain a transparent record of funding decisions, conditions, changes and accountable owners. . Track the relationship between capital consumed, capabilities delivered, adoption achieved and benefits realized. . . Expense, Vendor and Consulting Management. . Manage the transformation portfolio view of software licenses, subscriptions, data expenses, external services, contractors and consulting arrangements. . Coordinate statements of work, purchase orders, contract financials, rate cards, milestones, invoices, accruals, renewals and termination dates with Procurement, Legal and initiative owners. . Assess consulting and vendor utilization against contracted deliverables, internal capability transfer, budget and measurable value. . Identify duplicate tools, unused licenses, overlapping consulting scopes and other opportunities to reduce or redirect expense. . Maintain forward visibility into contractual commitments, renewal decisions and exit costs. . . Management Information and Data Quality. . Establish the authoritative portfolio dataset and controls required for consistent reporting across finance, delivery, adoption and benefits. . Partner with source-system owners to improve data definitions, completeness, timeliness, reconciliation and lineage. . Automate recurring reporting and analysis where practical while maintaining appropriate review and control points. . . Ensure assumptions, manual adjustments and data limitations are transparent in management reporting. . Produce targeted analyses that identify performance drivers, emerging risks and opportunities for resource or funding reallocation. . . Team Leadership. . Lead, develop and set priorities for data analysts and financial analysts supporting the transformation portfolio. . Allocate analyst capacity across recurring reporting, planning cycles, initiative support, ad hoc analysis and executive requests. . Establish quality standards, review controls, documentation and cross-training to improve consistency and reduce key-person dependency. . Build team capability in financial analysis, data management, visualization, benefits realization, executive communication and business partnership. . Create a culture of constructive challenge, accuracy, responsiveness and accountability. . . Governance and Executive Support. . Prepare materials for transformation investment, portfolio and performance forums, including financial position, KPI performance, benefits, risks and decisions required. . Maintain the portfolio decision log for budget changes, funding reallocations, benefit changes and material performance interventions. . Partner with initiative owners to ensure that investment requests are complete, comparable and grounded in measurable outcomes. . Support the Chief Transformation Officer and strategic transformation executives with fact-based insight and recommendations. . . Experience and Qualifications. . 8+ years of progressive experience in financial planning and analysis, corporate finance, capital management, portfolio management, transformation performance, management information, consulting or related disciplines. . At least 3 years of people-management or substantial team-leadership experience, including responsibility for developing analysts and reviewing complex work products. . Proven experience managing capital and expense budgets, forecasts, vendor or consulting spend, accruals, variances and executive financial reporting. . Experience defining KPIs, managing benefits realization and integrating financial, operational and delivery data into decision-oriented reporting. . Strong analytical and data-management capability, including advanced spreadsheet skills and experience with financial, portfolio, visualization or business-intelligence tools. . Ability to challenge assumptions, reconcile inconsistent data, explain complex financial information clearly and influence senior stakeholders. . . Experience in wealth management, banking, asset servicing, financial services, technology or another highly regulated environment preferred. . Bachelor's degree in finance, accounting, economics, business, data analytics or a related field required; MBA, CPA, CFA or other relevant advanced credential preferred. . . Key Success Measures. . Accurate and timely portfolio forecasts with reduced unexplained variance. . High utilization of approved capital and early identification of at-risk or stranded funding. . Clear linkage among investment, delivery, adoption and realized benefits. . Consistent KPI definitions and trusted executive reporting across the portfolio. . Reduced duplicate, unused or low-value vendor, consulting and software expense. . Timely interventions for initiatives that are off plan or not delivering expected value. . A high-performing analyst team with strong controls, documentation and succession capacity. . . Leadership Scope. . The manager will have direct responsibility for a team of data and financial analysts. The initial team size may evolve with the transformation portfolio. The role is expected to operate as both a people leader and a working manager, with direct involvement in planning, analysis, portfolio reviews and senior-management deliverables. . . Salary Range:. $137,400 - 233,600 USD. Salary range is a good faith estimate of base pay. Northern Trust provides a comprehensive benefits package including retirement benefits (401k and pension), health and welfare benefits (medical, dental, vision, spending accounts and disability), paid time off, parental and caregiver leave, life & accident insurance, and other voluntary and well-being benefits. Northern Trust also provides a discretionary bonus program that may include an equity component. . Work Authorization. . Applicants must be authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for employment-based visa sponsorship now or in the future. Northern Trust will not sponsor applicants for U.S. work visa status for this opportunity (no sponsorship is available for H-1B, L-1, TN, O-1, E-3, H-1B1, F-1, J-1, OPT, CPT or any other employment-based visa). . Build effective relationships across business, risk, compliance, legal, operations, technology and other partner groups.. Support communications, training and engagement activity that promotes consistent adoption of the RCM process across the organization.. . Continuous improvement and agile support. Ability to work autonomously within established procedures while recognizing when to seek guidance or escalate.. An agile, nimble and improvement-oriented mindset, with the flexibility to adapt quickly and support work beyond the core remit when priorities require it.. . Experience and qualifications. A college or university degree, or equivalent relevant work experience, is required.. Related Industry qualification / or studying towards, is preferred. 1-3 years' experience working in the financial services industry. Demonstrated experience producing accurate reporting or management information and maintaining structured data, records or repositories.. The Chief Bank Portfolio & Balance Sheet Hedging Manager is a senior leader within Corporate Treasury responsible for the strategic management of the firm's global bank investment portfolio and balance sheet interest-rate hedging activities. Reporting directly to the Treasurer, the role establishes and executes the investment and hedging strategy for Treasury-managed assets and structural balance sheet exposures, with the objectives of optimizing net interest income (NII), economic value, liquidity, capital efficiency, and risk-adjusted returns within the firm's approved risk appetite and regulatory requirements. The role serves as the Treasurer's principal executive for translating the firm's balance sheet, liquidity, interest-rate, deposit, and macroeconomic outlook into an integrated investment and hedging strategy. This leader will partner closely with Asset-Liability Management, Liquidity Management, Capital Management, Finance, Risk, Markets, Economics, and business-line senior stakeholders to ensure that investment portfolio and hedging decisions are aligned with the firm's broader balance sheet strategy.. Key Responsibilities. 1. Portfolio Strategy & Management. Lead strategy, construction, and management of the firm's Treasury investment portfolio, optimizing yield, liquidity, duration, capital efficiency, accounting outcomes, and risk-adjusted returns across approved asset classes and portfolio classifications. 2. Structural Interest-Rate Hedging. Own the design and execution of Treasury's structural hedging program, translating balance sheet exposures into hedge strategies that manage duration, repricing risk, NII volatility, economic value sensitivity, and accounting outcomes. 3. NII, ALM & Risk Optimization. Support sustainable NII and margin performance while partnering with ALM to manage interest-rate risk across NII sensitivity, EVE, DV01/PV01, key-rate exposures, deposit behavior, basis risk, optionality, and stress scenarios. 4. Liquidity, Capital & Accounting Management. Ensure investment and hedge strategies support liquidity resilience, HQLA, LCR/NSFR, monetization capacity, capital efficiency, RWA, AOCI/OCI, hedge accounting, and regulatory expectations. 5. Market Strategy, Execution & Governance. Serve as Treasury's senior market strategist and execution leader, translating macro, rate, yield-curve, liquidity, and credit-market views into portfolio and hedge actions while ensuring disciplined execution, controls, policies, limits, and senior governance communication. 6. Analytics, Performance & Scenario Management. Establish forward-looking analytics, stress testing, scenario analysis, and performance attribution covering market movements, portfolio positioning, funding changes, hedge effectiveness, liquidity value, capital utilization, NII-at-risk, EVE sensitivity, and risk-adjusted return. 7. Leadership & Organization. Build and lead a high-performing global Treasury investment and hedging organization with clear accountability, strong talent development, succession planning, cross-functional collaboration, analytical rigor, disciplined risk management, and effective controls. 8. Decision Authorities. Subject to delegated authorities, recommend and/or execute decisions across asset allocation, duration, yield-curve and sector positioning, investment timing, securities transactions, hedge size, tenor and instrument selection, reinvestment strategy, liquidity positioning, and risk-limit utilization; escalate material strategic changes to the Treasurer and appropriate governance committees.. The successful candidate will work closely with borrowers, broker-dealers, swap counterparties, and various internal functions. The role requires a strong understanding of equity markets, agency securities lending, equity finance, collateral optimisation, corporate actions, total return swaps, and the risk management framework required to support a client-focused, securities finance programme.. The key responsibilities of the role include:. . Agency Securities Lending Trading:. Manage day-to-day trading activity across an institutional equity securities lending portfolio, with responsibility for maximising client revenue while operating within approved risk, collateral, liquidity and counterparty guidelines. Develop and maintain strong relationships with borrowers, including prime brokers, banks and market intermediaries, to optimise lending demand and portfolio performance. Identify and monetise intrinsic lending opportunities across general collateral, specials, corporate actions, index events, rights issues, tender offers, and other market-driven demand opportunities. Monitor utilisation, fee levels, borrower demand, short interest, market liquidity, collateral usage and revenue performance to ensure the lending portfolio is optimised on a risk-adjusted basis. Partner with sales, client executives and product teams to identify and build incremental lending opportunities, support client reviews and contribute to new business opportunities. Prepare market commentary, trading colour, performance attribution and management reporting for internal stakeholders, beneficial owners and prospective clients. Ensure all trading activity meets best execution, fiduciary, counterparty credit and client guideline requirements.. Equity Total Return Swap Trading:. Support the continuous build-out, execution and management of an equity total return swap product offering for institutional and alternative investment clients. Comparable VP equity swap roles involve acting as the primary point of contact for top-tier funds, managing swap trading books, and supporting the development of local or regional swap offerings. Price, book, monitor and manage equity swap transactions across client portfolios, ensuring trades are aligned with client guidelines, internal risk limits and applicable market regulations. Monitor and manage financial risk within the equity swap trading book, including delta exposure, financing risk, dividend exposure, corporate action risk, liquidity risk, counterparty exposure and P&L volatility. Ensure swap and hedge bookings are accurately captured and reconciled, with daily P&L, delta and exception reporting reviewed and resolved on a timely basis. Coordinate with sales and relationship managers to help support client onboarding, trade execution, lifecycle management, resets, unwinds, amendments and ongoing service requirements. Work with operations, technology, legal, risk and compliance teams to enhance the equity swap platform, improve workflow automation, strengthen controls and support product scalability. Contribute to product development, including new market access, financing structures, pricing frameworks, client reporting and operating model enhancements.. Risk, Control and Governance:. Operate within a robust control framework covering client guidelines, counterparty credit limits, collateral eligibility, margin requirements, best execution, fiduciary standards and regulatory obligations. Partner with risk management to monitor portfolio exposures, trading concentrations, borrower limits, collateral quality and capital usage. Ensure accurate trade booking, settlement, billing, reconciliation, lifecycle event processing and exception management across both securities lending and equity swap activity.. Skills/Qualifications:. . The successful candidate will benefit from having :. . Required Experience:. Extensive experience across securities lending, equity finance, prime brokerage and/or synthetic financing. Demonstrated ability to generate revenue and improve portfolio performance within a controlled trading environment. Strong understanding of equity markets, borrow demand, specials, corporate actions, collateral mechanics, margining, trade lifecycle events and securities finance economics. Role Overview. . The KYC Periodic Reviews Team Lead is accountable for the end to end operational delivery of KYC activities within the KYC CoE. The role ensures KYC outputs are timely, accurate, and compliant, while embedding strong first line controls, effective issue management, and continuous improvement across KYC operations.. Ensure operational execution aligns with AML/KYC policies, procedures, regulatory requirements, and enterprise standards. Act as a point of escalation for complex KYC cases, operational issues, and delivery risks. Embed strong 1LOD controls across KYC operational processes to ensure consistent, high quality outputs. Identify, assess, and manage operational AML/KYC risks, ensuring issues are logged, tracked, and remediated in line with Northern Trust's risk appetite. Own and deliver remediation actions arising from quality assurance reviews, audits, regulatory exams, and 2LOD challenges. Drive root cause analysis for recurring issues and implement sustainable process improvements. Partner closely with the KYC CoE Governance, Quality Assurance, Training, and 2LOD teams to ensure alignment. Provide operational updates, MI, and insights to senior management, highlighting risks, capacity constraints, and emerging themes. Participate in relevant AML/KYC forums and working groups, representing KYC Operations and ensuring clear communication of operational risks and dependencies. Support the implementation of process enhancements, technology changes, and strategic initiatives impacting KYC Operations (e.g. tooling, workflow optimisation, regulatory change). Promote standardisation and best practices across the KYC CoE to drive efficiency and consistency. Champion a culture of continuous improvement, accountability, and operational excellence. Recruit, develop, and lead a team of KYC Operations professionals. Set clear performance expectations, provide coaching, and support capability development. Foster a collaborative, inclusive, and high performance culture aligned to Northern Trust values. The ideal candidate should have a fair amount of the following skills & experience:. Strong knowledge of AML/KYC regulations, customer due diligence requirements, and operational KYC processes. Proven experience in a KYC Operations, AML Operations, or Financial Crime role within Financial Services. Demonstrated people management experience, including performance management and capability development. Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage competing priorities in a high volume environment. Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to escalate and influence effectively. Strong risk management mindset with the ability to manage complex issues. College or university degree and / or equivalent relevant professional experience. . Work Authorization. . description: Director, Compliance, AMLCO - Sydney, Australia. . T he Director, AML Compliance, AMLCO (otherwise known as Money Laundering Reporting Officer or MLRO) serves as WUFSA's formally appointed Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing (AML/CTF) Compliance Officer as mandated by and defined under the Australian AML/CTF regulatory framework. . The role is responsible for leading the Australian AML/CTF compliance function, overseeing and coordinating the implementation and ongoing effectiveness of WUFSA's AML/CTF Program, ensuring compliance with applicable AML/CTF legislative and regulatory requirements, and supporting the identification, assessment, monitoring and management of money laundering, terrorism financing, proliferation financing, sanctions and other financial crime risks across the business.. The role provides strategic oversight, leadership and subject matter expertise of AML/CTF governance, risk assessment, monitoring, controls, training and regulatory compliance activities. The role is responsible for ensuring AML/CTF risk considerations are embedded into business decision-making, new products, services, delivery channels and strategic initiatives. The incumbent also provides independent challenge and oversight to ensure financial crime risks are appropriately identified, assessed, managed and escalated across the organisation.. While primarily focused on the Australian AML/CTF regulatory framework, the role is expected to lead regional AML/CTF projects across APAC, providing subject matter expertise, guidance and coaching to AML/CTF Compliance Officers and MLROs across the region.. Role Responsibilities. . REGULATORY APPOINTMENT REQUIREMENTS:. This position is the designated AML/CTF Compliance Officer for WUFSA.. The AML/CTF Compliance Officer has direct access to the WUFSA Governing Body and may escalate material AML/CTF matters independently of operational management where required to fulfil regulatory obligations. The role is responsible for maintaining an effective AML/CTF governance framework and ensuring AML/CTF obligations are communicated, implemented and monitored across the organisation.. The position holder shall:. . Serve as the nominated AML/CTF Compliance Officer for WUFSA. Act as primary contact with AUSTRAC regarding AML/CTF matters. Oversee and coordinate day-to-day compliance with AML/CTF legislation (comprises the Act, Rules and other applicable regulatory guidance and requirements), applicable sanctions obligations; WUFSA AML/CTF Program and WU global AML/CTF standards. Oversee the effectiveness of AML/CTF governance, risk management, and compliance controls. Escalate material AML/CTF risks, breaches and deficiencies to Senior Management and the Governing Body. Provide periodic AML/CTF reporting to Senior Management and relevant governance forums. Formally report AML/CTF compliance outcomes and program effectiveness to the Governing Body at least annually. Maintain eligibility to perform the role throughout tenure. Meet all competency, authority, and independence, and fit-and-proper requirements established under WUFSA's AML/CTF Program and associated governance framework. . AML/CTF Program Governance and Oversight. Own and oversee the WUFSA AML/CTF Program. Maintain AML/CTF policies, procedures, controls and governance documentation. Ensure AML/CTF frameworks remain aligned with legislative requirements and regulatory expectations. Oversee implementation of AML/CTF controls across all designated services. Ensure AML/CTF documentation remains fit for purpose and current. Coordinate periodic reviews and updates of the AML/CTF Program. Oversee remediation of compliance deficiencies, audit findings and regulatory issues. . AML/CTF Compliance Officer and MLRO Responsibilities. Perform statutory responsibilities of the AML/CTF Compliance Officer. Act as the principal AML/CTF contact with AUSTRAC. Ensure compliance with all AML/CTF reporting obligations, including Suspicious Matter Reports (SMRs), Threshold Transaction Reports (TTRs), International Funds Transfer Instructions (IFTIs) and other regulatory reporting requirements. Oversee suspicious activity investigations, decision-making and escalation processes. Oversee the effectiveness of Customer Identification Program (CIP), Customer Due Diligence (CDD), Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) and ongoing customer monitoring controls. Ensure AML/CTF risk considerations are incorporated into new products, services, systems, delivery channels and material business change initiatives. Oversee sanctions compliance controls and escalation of potential sanctions-related matters. Ensure AML/CTF record-keeping obligations are maintained and periodically tested. Oversee implementation and monitoring of remediation programs arising from audits, compliance reviews, regulatory examinations and issue management activities. Maintain regulatory documentation, appointment records and compliance evidence. Support regulatory examinations, inspections, enquiries and information requests. Maintain awareness of emerging financial crime typologies, regulatory developments, sanctions risks and industry best practices. Ensure the organisation's AML/CTF obligations are effectively communicated and understood across relevant business areas. . Financial Crime Risk Management. Oversee the effective design and execution of enterprise AML/CTF risk assessments including associated customer, product, channel and geographic risk assessments. Ensure effective management of financial crime risks including money laundering, terrorism financing, proliferation financing, sanctions, and fraud, based on risk assessment outcomes and controls being implemented to manage the identified risks. Ensure enhanced due diligence requirements are effectively implemented. Review and appropriately challenge other business risk assessments as required. Escalate material financial crime risks to senior management and governance forums. . Governance, Board Reporting and Regulatory Engagement. Prepare periodic AML/CTF compliance reporting for Senior Management, Governing Body and other governance forums. Retain ownership and control of AML/CTF Compliance Officer reports and recommendations provided to the Governing Body, ensuring material findings, risks and recommendations are communicated transparently and without inappropriate modification. Provide formal AML/CTF Compliance Officer reporting to the Governing Body at least annually, including:. · Compliance with AML/CTF policies and procedures;. · Effectiveness of AML/CTF controls in managing ML/TF risks;. · Compliance with AML/CTF legislative and regulatory obligations;. · Material AML/CTF deficiencies, breaches and remediation activities. Escalate material AML/CTF incidents, compliance breaches, significant control deficiencies, emerging regulatory concerns and material financial crime risks as required. Present significant compliance issues, regulatory developments, financial crime trends, breaches and emerging risks to governance forums and senior stakeholders. Oversee responses to internal / external audit, compliance review, independent evaluation and regulatory findings. Monitor closure of audit, regulatory and review findings and ensure timely remediation of identified issues. Maintain effective relationships with regulators, governance stakeholders and relevant internal control functions. Provide strategic advice and independent challenge to support informed decision-making regarding AML/CTF and financial crime risk matters. Ensure Senior Management and the Governing Body remain informed of the effectiveness of the AML/CTF Program and material financial crime risks. . Monitoring, Training and Program Enhancement. Oversee AML/CTF compliance monitoring activities. Ensure AML/CTF training programs remain effective, current and risk based. Promote and maintain a strong financial crime compliance culture throughout the organisation. Coordinate independent review and evaluation of the AML/CTF Program at prescribed intervals. Monitor remediation and closure of findings arising from independent reviews. Report progress of remediation activities to Senior Management and the Governing Body. Assess emerging regulatory developments and recommend enhancements to AML/CTF controls and governance arrangements. Drive continuous improvement initiatives across financial crime compliance frameworks, systems and controls. Support the development of AML/CTF capability, awareness and expertise across the organisation. . AML/CTF Governance, Appointment and Regulatory Oversight. Maintain ongoing eligibility and suitability as the appointed AML/CTF Compliance Officer and MLRO. Support periodic Fit and Proper assessments and eligibility reviews. Maintain records evidencing appointment, eligibility and ongoing suitability. Ensure regulatory notifications relating to appointment, resignation, replacement or eligibility changes are completed within prescribed timeframes. Escalate any matter affecting continued eligibility, suitability, independence or regulatory standing. Ensure governance records relating to appointment remain current and available for review. Customer Focus Provides expert compliance support and guidance to business stakeholders while ensuring customer outcomes are balanced with regulatory obligations and risk management requirements.. Management & Planning Develops, oversees and enhances compliance frameworks, governance structures, policies and risk management programs.. Business Expertise Possesses extensive expertise in AML/CTF compliance, financial crime risk management, sanctions compliance and regulatory governance.. Leadership Provides strategic compliance leadership, influences senior stakeholders and drives a culture of accountability, integrity and regulatory compliance.. . Core Factors:. . Functional Knowledge. . Recognised subject matter expert in AML/CTF legislation, financial crime compliance, sanctions compliance, governance and regulatory engagement. Applies deep technical expertise and judgement to oversee AML/CTF risk management frameworks and regulatory compliance obligations. Possesses extensive knowledge of money laundering, terrorism financing, proliferation financing and sanctions risks relevant to financial services and payments industries. Maintains awareness of emerging financial crime typologies, regulatory developments, industry trends and best practices. Provides authoritative advice to Senior Management, governance forums and business stakeholders regarding AML/CTF obligations and financial crime risk management. Exercises independent judgement in complex and high-risk regulatory and compliance matters. Influences organisational strategy, governance and risk management outcomes through expert knowledge and thought leadership. Area of Impact. . Direct impact on WUFSA's regulatory compliance, financial crime risk profile, governance effectiveness and regulatory relationships.. Nature of Impact. . Influences organizational compliance, risk management and regulatory outcomes through independent oversight and governance leadership. Problem Solving. . Exercises independent judgement and advanced analytical skills to address complex regulatory, governance and financial crime matters.. MANDATORY ELIGIBILITY AND APPOINTMENT REQUIREMENTS. The incumbent must be an Australian resident and satisfy the eligibility requirements for appointment as an AML/CTF Compliance Officer under applicable AML/CTF legislation.. Competence and Capability. The incumbent will demonstrate:. Advanced knowledge of AML/CTF legislation, regulatory requirements and industry guidance. Strong understanding of money laundering, terrorism financing, proliferation financing and sanctions risks. Ability to interpret and apply complex regulatory obligations and expectations. Experience designing, implementing and overseeing AML/CTF compliance frameworks. Experience engaging with regulators, governance forums, internal audit and external audit. Capability to exercise independent judgement and risk-based decision-making. Ability to effectively challenge business decisions where AML/CTF risks or compliance concerns exist. Capability to oversee AML/CTF governance, compliance monitoring, reporting and risk management activities.. Authority. The incumbent will:. Hold a management-level position or equivalent authority within the organisation. Possess sufficient standing and influence to drive compliance outcomes across the business. Have unrestricted access to Senior Management and the Governing Body. Maintain direct access to the Governing Body and appropriate governance forums for the purpose of escalating AML/CTF matters independently of operational management. Have authority to independently escalate ML/TF risks, deficiencies, breaches and regulatory concerns. Have authority to challenge business decisions where AML/CTF risks are not being appropriately addressed. Have authority to directly engage and communicate with AUSTRAC and other relevant regulators regarding AML/CTF matters where required. Have unrestricted access to governance committees and the Governing Body to discharge AML/CTF Compliance Officer responsibilities. Have authority to request information, documentation and resources necessary to effectively discharge AML/CTF obligations. Be empowered to recommend corrective actions, control enhancements and remediation initiatives to address identified AML/CTF risks and compliance deficiencies. Independence. The incumbent will:. Operate independently and objectively in the performance of AML/CTF Compliance Officer responsibilities. Remain free from undue operational influence or conflicts that may impair independent judgement. Exercise independent judgement regarding AML/CTF risk management and compliance matters. Escalate AML/CTF concerns without inappropriate influence or restriction. Maintain sufficient independence to provide objective oversight, challenge and governance across the AML/CTF Program. Access to Resources. The incumbent will have access to:. Appropriate staffing resources and subject matter expertise. AML/CTF systems, technology and reporting tools. Legal, compliance and risk management support functions. External professional advice where necessary. Information necessary to discharge responsibilities effectively. Ongoing training and development necessary to maintain AML/CTF competency. Appropriate organisational support, budget and resources to enable effective execution of AML/CTF responsibilities. Immediately disclose any matter that could impact ongoing suitability, independence or effectiveness in the role. Continue to satisfy WUFSA's AML/CTF Compliance Officer eligibility and Fit and Proper requirements. Failure to maintain these requirements may result in the incumbent no longer being eligible to perform the role of AML/CTF Compliance Officer and MLRO.. FIT AND PROPER ASSESSMENT REQUIREMENTS. The incumbent must immediately disclose any matter that may impact suitability including:. criminal investigations or proceedings;. regulatory investigations or actions;. disciplinary actions;. material conflicts of interest;. insolvency-related matters;. any circumstance that could affect integrity, competence, independence or suitability. Financial probity assessments where permitted under applicable laws. Review of competency, performance and regulatory obligations associated with the role. Conflicts of Interest. The incumbent must disclose any actual, potential or perceived conflict of interest which may impair their independence, objectivity or ability to perform AML/CTF Compliance Officer responsibilities. WUFSA may conduct periodic reassessments of the incumbent's Fit and Proper status. Continued appointment is contingent upon maintaining satisfactory Fit and Proper standing.. Role Requirements. . Minimum 10 years' experience in AML/CTF Compliance, Financial Crime Compliance, Financial Crime Risk Management, Regulatory Compliance or related disciplines. undefined. title: Manager Paralegal - Corporate Governance
location: USA NY - New York - 80 Pine Street; USA GA - Atlanta - Corporate Center V, 5 Concourse Parkway, Suite 2300
description: At Western Union, we're more than a trusted name in global payments. We're moving beyond remittances, beyond cash, and beyond the expectations of our customers. Our talented teams enable us to transform into a digital-first company, built on the strength of our retail foundation and powered by next-generation payments. All this with the goal of helping people prosper. Our customers inspire us to push boundaries and create services that make life easier and communities stronger. Wherever you are in the world, we're committed to shaping the next generation of financial experiences. Join us as we go beyond and be part of a team that's redefining what's possible.. The Manager, Corporate Governance Paralegal is an experienced legal professional who provides high-level support for the Company's public company governance, Board and committee administration, securities compliance, and domestic and international subsidiary management activities. Working with limited supervision, this role manages recurring governance processes, coordinates complex and time-sensitive workstreams, maintains accurate corporate records, and serves as a key liaison among Legal, senior management, Finance, Tax, Treasury, Investor Relations, Human Resources, external counsel, registered agents, and other service providers. The Manager also helps develop scalable procedures, technology solutions, and controls that promote timely , accurate , and consistent execution of the corporate governance function. Also likely to support other workstreams within the Corporate Legal Affairs group, including across litigation, public policy, and human resou rce. May be involved in helping others develop guidelines, policies or procedures and would have some authority to deviate from existing policies and procedures. May provide recommendations, guidance and training on more advanced subject-matter to various levels of employees. . Key Responsibilities. . Subsidiary Management. . Manage governance and compliance activities for a portfolio of domestic and international subsidiaries and other legal entities. Prepare and coordinate organizational documents, Board and shareholder actions, officer and director appointments, annual meeting materials, powers of attorney, certificates, incumbency documents, and related records. Maintain entity minute books, ownership records, organizational charts, officer and director rosters, registered-office information, and other corporate data. Administer the legal entity management system and promote data integrity through regular audits, reconciliations, standardized naming conventions, and documented controls. Track annual reports, franchise and similar filings, licenses, good-standing requirements, and other recurring statutory obligations, coordinating with local teams, registered agents, and external counsel. Support entity formations, qualifications, reorganizations, mergers, conversions, dissolutions, name changes, capital actions, and intercompany transactions. Coordinate document execution, notarization, legalization, apostille, certification, and filing requirements across jurisdictions. . Provide corporate records and governance support for financings , audits, tax matters, regulatory examinations, due diligence, and strategic transactions. . Identify opportunities to simplify and automate recurring processes and enhance the effective use of Board portals, entity management systems, filing platforms, electronic signature tools, and document repositories. Manage vendor relationships, invoices, budgets, and service performance within assigned areas. . . General Corporate Governance Support. . Assist with managing annual and recurring governance calendars for the Board of Directors and its committees and the Boards of Directors for regulated subsidiaries , including meeting schedules, approvals, deliverables, and filing deadlines. Assist with coordination of Board and committee meeting processes and logistics , including preparation and distribution of agendas, materials, resolutions, written consents, minutes, and action-item trackers , and hotel, transportation, dinner, and other meeting logistics. . Support maintenance of official Board and committee records, governance policies, committee charters, director and officer information, delegations of authority, and related corporate records. Support director onboarding, orientation, continuing education, evaluations, independence reviews, and annual director and officer questionnaires. Assist with the annual meeting of stockholders, including planning, documentation, meeting logistics , voting materials, and maintenance of the official record. Assist with compliance with applicable securities laws and stock exchange requirements and monitor developments affecting public company governance practices. Assist with the preparation, review, coordination, and filing of periodic and current reports, proxy materials, registration statements, and Section 16 reports, as assigned. Maintain the corporate governance section of the Company's external website and support governance-related disclosures and records retention. . Handle sensitive and privileged information with discretion and exercise sound judgment in interactions with directors, executives, and other stakeholders. Perform other corporate governance, securities, and legal department responsibilities as assigned. . . . Basic Qualifications. 8+ years of corporate paralegal or corporate governance experience, including meaningful experience supporting a U.S. public company. Bachelor's degree and/or an ABA-approved paralegal certificate. Demonstrated experience with Board and committee administration, corporate records, and legal entity management. Working knowledge of public company governance practices, Delaware corporate law concepts, SEC reporting processes, Section 16 requirements, and applicable NYSE or Nasdaq standards. Experience with Board portals, entity management systems, SEC filing platforms, electronic signature tools, and Microsoft applications. Prior experience leading projects, coordinating work, mentoring colleagues, or overseeing service providers.. Preferred:. Experience supporting a global subsidiary portfolio is strongly preferred. Direct people-management experience is preferred.. Skills and Competencies. . Exceptional organization, attention to detail, and commitment to accurate and complete records. Ability to manage multiple high-priority matters, anticipate deadlines, and deliver under compressed timeframes. . Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to draft clear governance documents and communicate effectively with senior leaders. Sound judgment, discretion, professionalism, and the ability to work independently while recognizing when legal review or escalation is required. . Strong collaboration and stakeholder-management skills across functions, geographies, and levels of seniority. Analytical and process-oriented mindset, with a focus on controls, consistency, efficiency, and continuous improvement. Commitment to integrity, confidentiality, accountability, and high-quality client service. . . We make financial services accessible to humans everywhere. Join us for what 's next. Western Union is well positioned to become the world's most accessible financial services company -transforming lives and communities. More than moving money, we design easy-to-use products and services for our digital and physical financial ecosystem that help our customers move forward. Just as we help our global customers prosper, we support our employees in achieving their professional aspirations. You'll have plenty of opportunities to learn new skills and build a career, as well as receive a great compensation package. If you're ready to help drive the future of financial services, it's time for Western Union. Learn more about our purpose and people at https://careers.westernunion.com/. . WORK LOCATION. . HYBRID - Western Union values in-person collaboration, problem solving, and ideation whenever possible. Document and/or refer specific cases for further investigation. Participate in team efforts such as huddles, problem solving, training, and innovation efforts of the team, FIU, and Western Union.. location: USA NY - New York - 80 Pine Street
description: Western Union Digital is on a mission to transform a 175+ year-old global brand into the next generation of financial services. Serving customers across 30+ countries, we are building trusted, delightful digital experiences that help people move and manage money anywhere in the world. We are seeking a Director of Product Management to define product vision, set strategy, and drive execution across our North American Digital business. This is a high-impact leadership role that balances long-term vision with hands-on execution. You will shape the future of our core remittance experience while expanding into adjacent financial services that deepen customer relationships and increase lifetime value.. You will combine customer obsession, strategic thinking, data-driven decision making, and exceptional cross-functional leadership to accelerate growth, improve retention, and deliver category-leading customer experiences. As a key member of the Digital leadership team, you will be responsible for defining priorities, developing product leaders, and delivering measurable business outcomes across one of Western Union's most important growth markets.. Key Responsibilities. Define and Lead US Digital Product Strategy. Own the vision, roadmap, and execution strategy for the North American Digital business, driving both the core remittance experience and the evolution into adjacent financial services, including wallets, banking, and other customer solutions that expand engagement and lifetime value. Drive Customer Growth: Accelerate customer acquisition through best-in-class onboarding, referral programs, localized customer experiences, experimentation, and continuous funnel optimization across key US sending corridors.. Increase Retention and Customer Engagement: Build delightful, trusted experiences that strengthen customer loyalty by reducing friction, improving transparency, and enhancing key customer touchpoints including pricing, network coverage, reliability, delivery speed, and account management.. Build for High-Value Customers: Develop differentiated experiences for high-value senders through premium services, tailored verification journeys, loyalty programs, personalized experiences, and enhanced support offerings.. Expand Beyond Remittances: Identify, validate, and launch adjacent financial services that solve meaningful customer problems, deepen engagement, and create new growth opportunities beyond traditional money transfer.. description: About Payoneer. The Opportunity. This is a strategic programs role at the center of Global Sales HQ. You own the portfolio of sales-development programs and strategic sales initiatives that turn strategy into repeatable, measurable motions across regions - and you are the connective tissue between Sales and Product, between demand generation and closure, and between global standards and on-the-ground execution. In a matrixed organization where regional heads own their reps and delivery, you own the standard, the operating rhythm, and the cross-functional programs that make the whole sales engine more effective. It is a builder-strategist role: you design the programs, orchestrate the launches, instrument them, and scale what works. What You'll Own. SALES DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMS & STRATEGIC SALES INITIATIVES. Own the portfolio of sales-development programs and strategic initiatives that raise the productivity and consistency of the global sales organization, from skills and plays to new sales motions. Translate the annual sales strategy into a sequenced program roadmap with clear owners, milestones, and success metrics. Stand up initiatives as time-boxed programs with scale / iterate / kill decision gates, plus the governance rhythm - interlocks, exception desks, QBR cadences - that keeps regions on one standard. SALES - PRODUCT INTERLOCK. Own the operating interlock between Sales and Product: a structured, two-way loop that turns field signal into roadmap input and turns roadmap into sales readiness. Represent the voice of the field in prioritization, packaging, and pricing discussions, and carry product context back into the field. Ensure every material product change lands with the sales org through readiness, positioning, and enablement - nothing ships to market unsold internally. CAMPAIGNS - DEMAND & CLOSURE ALIGNMENT. Orchestrate integrated GTM campaigns that align top-of-funnel demand generation with the sales closure motion, so demand converts to pipeline and pipeline to revenue. Partner with Marketing and RevOps to define targeting, messaging, and the handoff and follow-up SLAs that connect demand to closure. Instrument campaigns end to end (demand → qualified pipeline → closed revenue) and drive continuous, data-led improvement. NEW PRODUCT INTRODUCTION (NPI) INTO MARKETS. Own the sales side of new-product introductions: the launch playbook, market-readiness criteria, and sequencing for introducing products into markets, countries, and corridors. Coordinate the cross-functional launch (Product, Marketing, Enablement, regional sales) so each introduction has clear ownership, ramp targets, and measurement. Define go / no-go gates and post-launch review so the organization scales winners and retires what doesn't land. COUNTRY & CORRIDOR SALES STRATEGY. Define where-to-play / how-to-win by country and corridor - grounded in market, revenue, and account data. Build and maintain the market and corridor tiering and prioritization that focuses sales investment on the highest-value opportunities. Partner with regional Sales heads to translate corridor strategy into coverage, targeting, and sequenced motions on the ground. What Success Looks Like - First 6-12 Months. A published, sequenced program roadmap tied to the sales strategy, with governance live and adopted across regions. A functioning Sales-Product interlock running on a regular cadence, with measurable roadmap and readiness outcomes. Integrated demand-to-closure campaigns live, with clean end-to-end metrics leadership uses to steer. A repeatable NPI launch model and an active country / corridor sales strategy directing prioritized investment. What You Bring. REQUIRED. 8+ years in GTM strategy, sales programs, sales enablement / excellence, or strategic sales initiatives, including running cross-functional programs at scale. Proven experience owning a Sales-Product interlock or equivalent alignment between the field and the product roadmap. A track record designing and launching go-to-market campaigns that connect demand generation to sales closure. Experience leading new-product introductions and / or market and corridor launch strategy. Strong analytical foundation - comfortable in the data, building market / corridor prioritization, and instrumenting funnels end to end. A record of operating in a matrixed, multi-region organization and driving alignment without direct authority; excellent executive communication. PREFERRED. Hands-on fluency with the modern sales stack - Salesforce, Gong, BI / SQL (BigQuery a plus), and campaign tooling. Familiarity with corridor-based, multi-currency GTM and with SMB / marketplace / platform segments. Experience standing up governance rhythms - interlocks, QBRs, and forecast operating models - across regions. . Fintech / payments experience strongly preferred. Background in fintech, payments, or cross-border B2B financial services. Understanding of how compliance, trust, long sales cycles, and multi-stakeholder buying committees shape GTM in regulated financial services. Comfort translating product complexity (multi-currency, FX, working capital, stablecoin rails) into simple, sellable, market-ready motions. Who You'll Work With. Product, Marketing, RevOps, regional sales heads (EMEA, APAC, LATAM), Sales Enablement & Excellence, Customer Retention & Expansion, and Strategic Accounts. You'll be a core member of the Global Sales HQ leadership team, reporting to the VP of Global Sales. Why Join. You'll own the programs and cross-functional interlocks that a global sales organization runs on - the layer where strategy, product, demand, and execution meet. You'll build, not just maintain, in a company at the frontier of cross-border payments, with the data, tooling, and executive support to make GTM measurably better across three regions. description: About Payoneer. We're a community with over 2,500 colleagues all over the world, working to serve customers, and partners in over 190 countries and territories. By taking the complexity out of the financial workflows-including everything from global payments and compliance to multi-currency and workforce management, to providing working capital and business intelligence-we give businesses the tools they need to work efficiently worldwide and grow with confidence.. About Payoneer Workforce Management (WFM). Payoneer Workforce Management (WFM) is Payoneer's global workforce solutions business, helping companies hire, onboard, pay, and manage talent anywhere in the world. The business enables organizations to build international teams quickly and compliantly without the need to establish legal entities in every country where they hire. As remote and distributed workforces become increasingly common, companies face challenges related to employment compliance, payroll, benefits administration, contractor management, and local labor regulations. Payoneer WFM simplifies these complexities through technology-enabled workforce solutions and in-country expertise. What We Do: Payoneer WFM provides end-to-end solutions that help businesses:. Engage and manage contractors compliantly. Process global payroll across multiple countries and currencies. Manage onboarding and offboarding processes. Ensure compliance with local employment and labor laws. Handle benefits administration and workforce operations. Support international expansion without requiring entity setup. Today, Payoneer WFM supports businesses across more than 160 countries, enabling them to access talent globally while maintaining compliance and operational efficiency. The platform enables businesses to:. Hire employees and contractors in 160+ countries. Run global payroll in 70+ currencies. Manage onboarding, contracts, benefits, compliance, expenses, and offboarding from a single platform. Navigate local labor laws, tax requirements, and employment regulations across jurisdictions. Employer of Record (EOR): A key offering within WFM is Employer of Record (EOR). Under the EOR model, Payoneer WFM becomes the legal employer of an individual in their local country while the client company manages the employee's day-to-day responsibilities, goals, and performance. This allows organizations to hire talent internationally without establishing a local subsidiary or legal entity. Payoneer WFM manages employment contracts, payroll, taxes, statutory benefits, and compliance requirements, enabling clients to focus on growing their business. Why This Market Matters: The global workforce landscape has changed significantly over the last few years. Companies are increasingly adopting remote and distributed hiring models, allowing them to access talent regardless of geography. As a result, the demand for global employment solutions, international payroll, and compliance management has grown rapidly. How WFM Fits Within Payoneer: Payoneer is widely recognized as a global financial technology company that enables businesses to send, receive, and manage cross-border payments worldwide. Workforce Management extends this mission by helping businesses not only move money globally but also hire and manage talent globally. Together, these solutions enable companies to build, operate, and scale international businesses more efficiently. Payoneer WFM is helping redefine how companies build global teams, making international hiring simpler, faster, and more accessible for businesses around the world. About the role:. We are looking for a detail-oriented and proactive Global HR Operations Specialist - Europe to join our team. In this role, you will be responsible for managing the end-to-end employee lifecycle - including onboarding, offboarding, query resolution, and compliance. You'll be a key player in ensuring smooth experiences for employees and clients across various geographies while maintaining adherence to local labor laws and SLAs. What you'll do -. Onboarding :. Manage end-to-end onboarding process of new employees, following internal Service Level Agreements (SLAs). Ensure all necessary paperwork, documents, compliance checks, and systems access are prepared compliantly for new hires. Provide ongoing support and act as the primary point of contact to provide guidance to new hires, addressing any questions that may arise. Offboarding:. Manage end-to-end offboarding process of new employees, following internal Service Level Agreements (SLAs). Act as the subject matter expertise to advise on the offboarding laws and regulations to ensure compliance. Coordinate with the payroll department and local vendors to ensure accurate final pay to the exit employees and timely deregistration. Collect and process all necessary exit documentation and return company assets. Coordinate with internal teams, clients, and third-party vendors to ensure seamless transitions. Trigger communication workflows and ensure document compliance. Employee Helpdesk Management:. Resolve HR-related help requests in a timely and empathetic manner. Collaborate cross-functionally with payroll, legal, and tech teams to resolve employee queries. Maintain documentation and response logs for audits and process improvements. Compliance & Labor Law Adherence:. Stay updated with L abour laws and statutory regulations in assigned countries. Ensure all HR processes and documentation are compliant with local employment laws. Work closely with legal teams to implement policy updates as needed. SLA Monitoring & Reporting:. Track service level agreements for onboarding/offboarding and help requests. Generate weekly/monthly reports on operational efficiency and issue resolution metrics. Identify process gaps and suggest continuous improvement initiatives. Who you are:. 6 years+ of experience in HR operations or employee lifecycle management. Strong understanding of EU Region HR processes and local labor laws. Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills. Comfortable working in a fast-paced, rapidly-changing global environment. Comfortable being in a client-facing role. Strong organizational skills. Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English. Nice-to-have:. Familiarity with HR systems (e.g., Zoho People, BambooHR, or similar). About Payoneer Workforce Management (WFM). Payoneer Workforce Management (WFM) is Payoneer's global workforce solutions business, helping companies hire, onboard, pay, and manage talent anywhere in the world. The business enables organizations to build international teams quickly and compliantly without the need to establish legal entities in every country where they hire. As remote and distributed workforces become increasingly common, companies face challenges related to employment compliance, payroll, benefits administration, contractor management, and local labor regulations. Payoneer WFM simplifies these complexities through technology-enabled workforce solutions and in-country expertise. What We Do: Payoneer WFM provides end-to-end solutions that help businesses:. Engage and manage contractors compliantly. Process global payroll across multiple countries and currencies. Manage onboarding and offboarding processes. Ensure compliance with local employment and labor laws. Handle benefits administration and workforce operations. Support international expansion without requiring entity setup. Today, Payoneer WFM supports businesses across more than 160 countries, enabling them to access talent globally while maintaining compliance and operational efficiency. The platform enables businesses to:. Hire employees and contractors in 160+ countries. Run global payroll in 70+ currencies. Manage onboarding, contracts, benefits, compliance, expenses, and offboarding from a single platform. Navigate local labor laws, tax requirements, and employment regulations across jurisdictions. Employer of Record (EOR): A key offering within WFM is Employer of Record (EOR). Under the EOR model, Payoneer WFM becomes the legal employer of an individual in their local country while the client company manages the employee's day-to-day responsibilities, goals, and performance. This allows organizations to hire talent internationally without establishing a local subsidiary or legal entity. Payoneer WFM manages employment contracts, payroll, taxes, statutory benefits, and compliance requirements, enabling clients to focus on growing their business. Why This Market Matters: The global workforce landscape has changed significantly over the last few years. Companies are increasingly adopting remote and distributed hiring models, allowing them to access talent regardless of geography. As a result, the demand for global employment solutions, international payroll, and compliance management has grown rapidly. Workforce Management extends this mission by helping businesses not only move money globally but also hire and manage talent globally.
